coverage.assessment: Four links break: the cutting is never handed over; Sir James's knowledge of Tommy's actions has no source; the 'put-up job' rationale is gone; and the premise that the treaty will be credited to Brown is cut before 'So no one will think...'. Separately, the partner 028 revision drops the policemen's-orders explanation. That is not charged to this chapter.

Three referent problems: 'this paragraph' has no antecedent; 'get him out of the way' loses its Beresford antecedent; 'frayed inner edges' loses the magazine page. The scene also jumps from the library to 'the square' with no drive.

Speaker turns stay clear through the reveal. Julius's drawl, Jane's 'Those papers were my trust,' and Sir James's measured lines are preserved. The cut recounting is treated as a knowledge problem under causality.
Sir James's theory stays in speech rather than narration. The 'no one has gone into the house' claim and the 'back as well' watch are kept, and 'Bown' is avoided.
The reveal is not premature. But the cut stealthy footstep removes an audible clue to the hidden pair. Dropping 'watching her' also flattens Sir James's sinister attention before he unmasks.

Tuppence's exultation ('They were going to win!'), 'No dummy this time!', and the 'Hark!... Absurd!' rhythm are lost. All three were present in the first draft. The climax pacing itself remains strong.
The triumph-then-reversal contrast is weakened because the confident build-up (exultation, 'he will not find us unprepared') is trimmed. The core double-mask irony survives.
All three dependencies have both endpoints present in the actual abridged texts. The 028 revision's loss of the policemen's orders is a partner-side gap, noted here only.

strengths: The unmasking sequence (paragraphs 29–31) keeps the exact ellipsis pacing from 'the presence of Mr. Brown' to 'In this room.... I am Mr. Brown'.
The ending keeps the signet ring, 'Ave, Cæsar!' still looking at Tommy, and the bitter almonds, so the death is rendered indirectly as planned.
The treaty is folded into his pocket-book, so Carter's retrieval in 028 connects.
Julius's drawling 'caught redhanded with the goods upon you' punctures the melodrama in character.
summary: The revision keeps the reveal spine intact: the verbatim lines, the pocket-book, the curtain fancy, the Tommy gaze, and the poison ending all survive. However, several trims made only in the revision cut necessary setup. The newspaper cutting is never shown, so 'this paragraph' dangles. Tuppence's account of the rescue is gone, so Sir James knows what Tommy did without being told. Smaller cuts weaken the staged-escape logic, the treaty-pocket reasoning, the move from library to Soho, and Tuppence's rising suspense in the house. Each can be fixed by restoring a short first-draft sentence.
